name: play-pause-morph
title: Play/pause icon morph
summary: A play button whose triangle morphs into two pause bars: pathTween interpolates between two four-point paths with a tween of {"value": "@playing", "anim": 0.35}, and a tap flips @playing.
prompt: A round play button that morphs smoothly into a pause icon when tapped, and back to play on the next tap.
teaches: Morph between two paths with pathTween {id, path1, path2, tween}, then draw the result by its id with drawPath
Animate the morph by making the tween an anim object: {"value": "@playing", "anim": 0.35}
Build both shapes with the same commands in the same order: the play triangle is split into two quads to match the two pause bars, corner for corner
pitfalls: The two paths must have the same verbs and point count, or the tween has nothing to pair up
An SVG string in resources.paths becomes an empty path in Java (U11): use the op list (moveTo/lineTo/close objects)
json2rc also accepts {"data": [...]} in resources.paths; Java throws a ClassCastException on it, so stay with the op list
The TS player does not draw pathTween results (EXAMPLES_FINDINGS T16)
Paths in resources.paths have fixed coordinates: centre them with one translate from componentWidth()/componentHeight() rather than drawing at the header's 180, 90

snippets.note: pathTween icon = play ↔ pause, tween {value: @playing, anim: 0.35}
play as two quads, ordered like the pause bars

check.describe: A tap at 0.1 s, captured 0.15 s later: halfway between play and pause, two slanted quads. Settles to two pause bars by 0.5 s. Resized (narrow 240, wide 540×260) the button and caption stay centred: one translate by (componentWidth() / 2 - 180, componentHeight() / 2 - 110) moves the whole drawing, so the paths keep their header coordinates.
